newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf has some improvement in Euro refining.
newsitem.headline: Elf has some improvement in Euro refining.

text.p: French oil group Elf Aquitaine said it had some improvement in European refining margins in 1996, up 19 percent to $2.67 per barrel, but this was offset by worsening marketing margins and by strikes in France.
"With European refining margins still very volatile, they did show some improvement in comparison to the historically low levels of 1995," Elf said in a statement.
"Nevertheless, the favourable effects of this improvement were offset by worsening marketing margins as well as the impact of strikes in France last December," it added.
It said that in Germany, the Minol service station network neared break-even at the end of 1998, ahead of schedule.
In France, the company adapted its structure to a market characterised by supermarket competition and refining over-capacity in Europe.
"Therefore, we are expecting a significant improvement in our results," Elf said in a statement.
Elf chief financial officer Bruno Weymuller said he did not expect restructuring charges in France in 1997 but he did not exclude them for Great Britain.
There, Elf signed a memorandum of understanding with Chevron 's Gulf and Murphy Oil Company unit Murco to rationalise their refining and marketing assets in the UK.
